summary: Kenyan taxi driver turned preacher Paul Mackenzie built a doomsday church that, from 2019 in the Shakahola Forest, ordered followers and their children to starve to death, leaving over 450 dead, while he took their money and land.

evidence.note: Birth given as possibly 1960 near Sultan Hamud; birthplace and year called uncertain
Ministry launched in 2003 among Malindi taxi drivers
MP alleges police bribery; repeated arrests and releases, 2017 raid frees 93 children
Host's theory that the Shakahola land sales were a real estate scam
Long segment on William Branham, his Kentucky youth, prophecies and 1977 end date
Mackenzie declares the Huduma Namba ID number the mark of the beast
Children ordered into a 40-day total fast and told to die first
Exhumed shallow graves of small children and whole families described
Death toll of at least 457, including 190 children, with hundreds missing
Followers urged to fast to death; rescued members charged with attempted suicide
Host jokes that young Mackenzie made dogs worship him and sometimes killed them
Burials called weddings to Jesus; host jokes about many child weddings

notes: Transcript dates birth to 1960 (late 30s in 1997) but later says he is in his 50s; kept 1960, approximate. From memory: spellings Mackenzie, Shakahola, Kwa Binzaro (transcript: Quabanzaro), guest Ify Nwadiwe, KE-14 Kilifi County for Malindi/Shakahola. Branham (secondary, long segment) sets covered start 1909. Child weddings mention is figurative (burial euphemism), kept per strict rule. Graphic-violence considered (strangling, clubbing) but brief.
